nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Market Scanning
nodes.summary: The capability to scan a universe of instruments, rank them by technical characteristics (momentum, volatility, ATR), and produce a focused watchlist for downstream analysis.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Feature Engineering
nodes.summary: The capability to calculate technical indicators from raw market data and assemble them into structured feature vectors for each watchlist candidate.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Snapshot Assembly
nodes.summary: The capability to assemble feature vectors into a deterministic Layer 2 Snapshot — the single source of truth consumed by all downstream systems.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Signal Generation
nodes.summary: The capability to apply strategy rules to Layer 2 Snapshots and produce actionable trade signals with conviction scores.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Order Management
nodes.summary: The capability to **execute an ADMITted paper decision**: take the ADMIT verdict from the runtime (Runtime Decision Record Schema, SCHEMA-012), apply a **fixed configured paper size** (ADR-011 D2 — adaptive position sizing is deferred), simulate (or, via the deferred Alpaca-paper adapter, place) the (paper) fill, and manage the order/fill lifecycle.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Stop-Loss Management
nodes.summary: The capability to place, monitor, and adjust stop-loss orders for all open positions using multiple stop types: fixed percentage, trailing, and floor-ratcheting.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Position Tracking
nodes.summary: The capability to track all open positions, monitor real-time P&L, detect position exits (fills, stops, manual closes), and maintain current portfolio state.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Guardrail Enforcement
nodes.summary: The capability to evaluate trade validation predicates, enforce quality gates, and issue approve/block decisions for every trade request from the Trading Engine.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Exposure Tracking
nodes.summary: The capability to calculate current portfolio exposure, detect threshold breaches, and trigger circuit-breaking behavior when risk limits are approached or exceeded.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: State Persistence
nodes.summary: The capability to read, write, and manage persistent memory files that enable stateless agent invocations to maintain continuity.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Context Assembly
nodes.summary: The capability to assemble the context window for each agent invocation within the token budget, prioritizing the most relevant information for the current task.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Trade Logging
nodes.summary: The capability to record structured trade journals for compliance, performance evaluation, and agent learning.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Performance Scoring
nodes.summary: The capability to calculate performance metrics from trade log data and produce evaluation scorecards that quantify strategy effectiveness.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Promotion Validation
nodes.summary: The capability to evaluate whether a strategy's scorecard meets promotion criteria and to manage the Paper Trading Promotion Gate that controls the PaperTrading → Validated lifecycle transition.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Decision Making
nodes.summary: The capability to score upgrade opportunities, select the best option under treasury constraints, and produce deterministic decision packets that govern system evolution.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Treasury Management
nodes.summary: The capability to track treasury budget, enforce spend policy (spendLimit, available balance), approve or deny upgrade spend requests, and record treasury deductions.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Upgrade Evaluation
nodes.summary: The capability to simulate upgrade outcomes, run paper trading for proposed changes, and evaluate whether upgrades actually improved the system using deterministic deltas.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Team Orchestration
nodes.summary: The capability to manage agent desk assignments, coordinate upgrade application across the agent team, and maintain team version state.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Market Regime Classification
nodes.summary: The capability to classify a single Layer-2-derived feature vector (SCHEMA-009) into exactly one deterministic macro-financial-conditions regime (SCHEMA-010), using only snapshot-local information.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Gold Decision Generation
nodes.summary: The capability to turn a Feature Vector (SCHEMA-009) + a Regime Classification (SCHEMA-010) into a deterministic, paper-trading **Gold DecisionPacket** (SCHEMA-011): a gold `direction` stance (the regime→direction policy) + `confidence`/`uncertainty` (the ADR-008 ordinal trust score) + the cited MOD-004 features + the L3 guard outcomes the packet honored.

nodes.label: Capability
nodes.name: Paper-Trade Admission
nodes.summary: The capability to **admit** a pure Gold DecisionPacket (SCHEMA-011) for paper trading against explicit runtime state — computing the stateful L3 guards Duplicate OK (`duplicate_ok`) + Operational OK (`operational_ok`), echoing the snapshot guards, and emitting an `ADMIT`/`HOLD`/`REJECT` Runtime Decision Record Schema (SCHEMA-012) plus a new ledger.

nodes.label: KnowledgeAsset
nodes.name: Event Sourcing
nodes.summary: The engineering principle that system state changes are captured as an immutable sequence of domain events rather than mutable state snapshots.

nodes.label: KnowledgeAsset
nodes.name: CQRS
nodes.summary: Command Query Responsibility Segregation — the engineering principle that the model used to read data (queries) should be separated from the model used to write data (commands).

nodes.label: KnowledgeAsset
nodes.name: Supervisor Pattern Methodology
nodes.summary: The engineering methodology where a meta-agent (supervisor) assembles, evaluates, and upgrades a team of specialized worker agents under resource constraints.

nodes.label: KnowledgeAsset
nodes.name: Office Action Methodology
nodes.summary: The engineering methodology of governing autonomous agent interventions through a deterministic state machine with explicit integration checkpoints, auditable transitions, and graceful degradation.

nodes.label: KnowledgeAsset
nodes.name: Guardrail Philosophy
nodes.summary: The engineering principle that autonomous agent autonomy MUST be preceded by hard, non-negotiable constraints that the agent cannot reason around.

nodes.label: KnowledgeAsset
nodes.name: Layer 2 Design Principles
nodes.summary: The engineering principles governing the Layer 2 (Strategy Engine / Analysis) snapshot system — the deterministic truth layer that bridges data ingestion (L1) and execution (L3).

nodes.label: KnowledgeAsset
nodes.name: Context Engineering
nodes.summary: The engineering principle that LLM agent context windows are finite resources that must be budgeted, prioritized, and managed like financial capital.

nodes.label: KnowledgeAsset
nodes.name: Agent Safety Principles
nodes.summary: The engineering guidance — derived from Anthropic's approach to AI safety in financial services and from the project's own risk model — that autonomous trading agents must be designed with multiple layers of safety: credential isolation, action constraints, self-verification, phased autonomy, and human oversight.

nodes.label: KnowledgeAsset
nodes.name: Stateless Agent Architecture
nodes.summary: The engineering principle that each agent invocation starts with zero inherent state.

nodes.label: KnowledgeAsset
nodes.name: Paper Trading Validation
nodes.summary: The engineering methodology that requires every trading strategy to pass simulated execution with real market data before live capital deployment.

nodes.label: KnowledgeAsset
nodes.name: Regime Taxonomy
nodes.summary: The engineering principle that a small, enumerated set of **market regimes** — deterministic, snapshot-local macro-financial-conditions states — should sit as a named abstraction layer between raw derived features and trade-decision logic.

nodes.label: Module
nodes.name: Guardrail Engine
nodes.summary: The code boundary that implements the Guardrail Enforcement capability: it evaluates a conjunction of hard-limit trade-validation predicates and returns a single approve/block decision plus the identity of the first failing predicate.

nodes.label: Module
nodes.name: Decision Engine
nodes.summary: The code boundary that implements the Decision Making capability: it scores candidate upgrades against current office weaknesses under treasury constraints and returns a deterministic decision packet selecting the best upgrade (or "no upgrade needed").

nodes.label: Module
nodes.name: Snapshot Consumer
nodes.summary: The Layer-3 ingestion boundary: the module that reads the Layer-2 truth snapshot (SCHEMA-001) via the Snapshot API (INT-001) and decides whether Layer 3 may act on it.

nodes.label: Module
nodes.name: Feature Builder
nodes.summary: The deterministic, snapshot-local transform that turns a validated `Snapshot` (from MOD-003) into a frozen feature vector (SCHEMA-009).

nodes.label: Module
nodes.name: Market Regime Classifier
nodes.summary: The deterministic, snapshot-local rule-selection engine that turns a Feature Vector (SCHEMA-009) into a frozen `RegimeClassification` (SCHEMA-010).

nodes.label: Module
nodes.name: Gold Decision Builder
nodes.summary: The deterministic, snapshot-local builder that turns a Feature Vector (SCHEMA-009) + a Regime Classification (SCHEMA-010) into a frozen, paper-only `GoldDecisionPacket` (SCHEMA-011).

nodes.label: Module
nodes.name: Paper-Trading Runtime
nodes.summary: The first **stateful** Layer-3 component: it consumes a pure Gold DecisionPacket v0 Schema (SCHEMA-011) plus explicit runtime state (a self-describing Runtime Ledger Schema + a versioned operational input) and emits a Runtime Decision Record Schema (SCHEMA-012) + a new ledger.

nodes.label: Module
nodes.name: Execution
nodes.summary: The first **money-shaped** Layer-3 module (ADR-011): it consumes an **ADMIT** Runtime Decision Record Schema (SCHEMA-012) + explicit portfolio state and produces an Execution Record Schema (SCHEMA-014) + a new Portfolio State Schema (SCHEMA-015).

nodes.label: Module
nodes.name: Gold Forward-Return Labeler
nodes.summary: A deterministic, **strictly-downstream, read-only** measurement module that labels each already-produced Gold DecisionPacket v0 Schema decision with the **gold return realized after its timestamp**, and aggregates the labels per regime × holding horizon.

nodes.label: Module
nodes.name: Chain Orchestrator
nodes.summary: The **end-to-end composition root** for Layer-3: it threads a banked Layer 2 Snapshot Schema (SCHEMA-001) through every already-governed stage in one deterministic call — `consume → build_features → classify → build_decision → evaluate → [GATE-001 guard] → execute → persist` — producing the full record set (Feature Vector Schema, Regime Classification Schema, Gold DecisionPacket v0 Schema, Runtime Decision Record Schema, Execution Record Schema) plus a new Runtime Ledger Schema + Portfolio State Schema.

nodes.label: Module
nodes.name: Operations Control Plane
nodes.summary: The `ops/` package — a **local terminal operator console** (a Textual TUI over a headless governed read-model) that observes the El Niño Layer-3 runtime and triggers operator actions in three safety tiers.

nodes.label: Pattern
nodes.name: Supervisor Pattern
nodes.summary: A meta-agent governs a team of specialized worker agents under resource constraints.

nodes.label: Pattern
nodes.name: Guardrail Pattern
nodes.summary: A validation checkpoint composed of boolean predicates that must ALL pass before an action is permitted.

nodes.label: Pattern
nodes.name: Evaluation Loop Pattern
nodes.summary: A cyclical pattern where system output is measured against defined metrics, scored into a structured scorecard, and fed back to governance for promotion or evolution decisions.

nodes.label: Pattern
nodes.name: Pipeline Pattern
nodes.summary: A linear sequence of processing stages where the output of each stage feeds as input to the next.

nodes.label: Pattern
nodes.name: Event Sourcing Pattern
nodes.summary: State changes are captured as an immutable, append-only sequence of domain events.

nodes.label: Pattern
nodes.name: Context Assembly Pattern
nodes.summary: A structured retrieval and assembly process that selects, prioritizes, and composes information into a bounded context window for a stateless agent invocation.

nodes.label: Pattern
nodes.name: Treasury Approval Pattern
nodes.summary: A two-gate financial approval process where resource spend requests must pass both a per-item limit check (spendLimit) and an available balance check before approval.

nodes.label: Pattern
nodes.name: Promotion Pattern
nodes.summary: A quantitative gate that controls promotion from a safe environment (paper trading) to a live environment (production).

nodes.label: Pattern
nodes.name: CQRS Pattern
nodes.summary: The read model (analytical snapshots) is separated from the write model (order execution).

nodes.label: Pattern
nodes.name: Multi-Agent Coordination Pattern
nodes.summary: Multiple specialized agents are organized into functional desks (Research, Strategy, Execution, Evaluator) under centralized coordination.

nodes.label: Pattern
nodes.name: Regime Classification Pattern
nodes.summary: A behavioral pattern that interposes a deterministic **semantic abstraction** step between measurement and action: ``` Snapshot → Features → [Semantic abstraction: regime] → Decision → Execution ``` A priority-ordered rule table maps a feature vector to exactly one enumerated regime (first match wins), projecting `matched_rule_id → regime`, and the decision layer reasons over the regime rather than the raw features.

nodes.label: Predicate
nodes.name: Position Size OK
nodes.summary: Boolean condition: `size <= min(current_equity * max_position_pct, max_trade_size)`.

nodes.label: Predicate
nodes.name: Daily Loss Cap OK
nodes.summary: Boolean condition: `daily_pnl > -daily_loss_cap`.

nodes.label: Predicate
nodes.name: Max Trades OK
nodes.summary: Boolean condition: `trades_today < max_trades_per_day`.

nodes.label: Predicate
nodes.name: Max Positions OK
nodes.summary: Boolean condition: `open_positions < max_positions`.

nodes.label: Predicate
nodes.name: Withdrawal Disabled
nodes.summary: Boolean condition: `not config.allow_withdrawals`.

nodes.label: Predicate
nodes.name: Duplicate OK
nodes.summary: Boolean L3 guard: `duplicate_ok` passes when the current `source_snapshot_id` has **not** already produced a Gold DecisionPacket (idempotency / de-duplication).

nodes.label: Predicate
nodes.name: Operational OK
nodes.summary: Boolean L3 guard: `operational_ok` passes when operational preconditions for acting on a gold decision hold — e.g.

nodes.label: Predicate
nodes.name: Cooldown OK
nodes.summary: Boolean L3 guard: `cooldown_ok` passes when at least `cooldown_window_hours` has elapsed — measured by the snapshot `as_of` (never wall-clock) — since the last **ADMIT** of a **different** snapshot.

nodes.label: ArtifactSchema
nodes.name: Layer 2 Snapshot Schema
nodes.summary: The foundational data contract of the whole system: the deterministic, versioned, self-contained analytical assessment the Layer-2 engine (Mr.

nodes.label: ArtifactSchema
nodes.name: Decision Packet Schema
nodes.summary: The data contract for the deterministic decision output of the Supervisor Office: the selected upgrade (or none), the ranked option set with scores and block reasons, the rationale, and the post-decision treasury state.

nodes.label: ArtifactSchema
nodes.name: Evaluation Scorecard Schema
nodes.summary: The performance-evidence contract the Supervisor Office consumes to decide whether — and how — to upgrade.

nodes.label: ArtifactSchema
nodes.name: Trade Validation Request Schema
nodes.summary: The data contract for a proposed-trade validation request submitted to the Risk Check API.

nodes.label: ArtifactSchema
nodes.name: Trade Validation Decision Schema
nodes.summary: The data contract for the approve/block decision returned by the Risk Check API after a trade-validation request is evaluated.

nodes.label: ArtifactSchema
nodes.name: Feature Vector Schema
nodes.summary: The deterministic output contract of the Feature Builder (MOD-004): a frozen, snapshot-local vector of features derived purely from a single Layer-2 Snapshot (SCHEMA-001), each carrying its provenance.

nodes.label: ArtifactSchema
nodes.name: Regime Classification Schema
nodes.summary: The deterministic output contract of the Market Regime Classifier (MOD-005): a frozen `RegimeClassification` derived purely from one Feature Vector (SCHEMA-009).

nodes.label: ArtifactSchema
nodes.name: Gold DecisionPacket v0 Schema
nodes.summary: The deterministic output contract of the Gold Decision Builder (MOD-006): a frozen `GoldDecisionPacket` derived purely from one Feature Vector (SCHEMA-009) + one Regime Classification (SCHEMA-010).

nodes.label: ArtifactSchema
nodes.name: Runtime Decision Record Schema
nodes.summary: The output contract of the paper-trading runtime's pure `evaluate()` (MOD-007): a frozen `RuntimeDecisionRecord` that **wraps** a pure Gold DecisionPacket v0 Schema (SCHEMA-011) by reference (`source_packet_id`) and carries the runtime's evaluated six-guard block plus a fail-closed `ADMIT`/`HOLD`/`REJECT` verdict.

nodes.label: ArtifactSchema
nodes.name: Runtime Ledger Schema
nodes.summary: The append-only, self-describing state artifact of the paper-trading runtime (MOD-007): a frozen `RuntimeLedger` of `LedgerEntry` records, keyed by `source_snapshot_id`.

nodes.label: ArtifactSchema
nodes.name: Execution Record Schema
nodes.summary: The output contract of the execution layer's pure `execute()`: a frozen `ExecutionRecord` that **wraps** an ADMIT Runtime Decision Record Schema (SCHEMA-012) by reference (`source_record_id`) and records the (paper) fill it produced + the guard provenance it passed.

nodes.label: ArtifactSchema
nodes.name: Portfolio State Schema
nodes.summary: The append-only, self-describing portfolio/position state of the execution layer: a frozen `PortfolioState` of per-instrument positions + an append-only `executions` history keyed by `source_snapshot_id`.

nodes.label: System
nodes.name: Data Pipeline
nodes.summary: Bounded context responsible for acquiring market data from external providers, engineering features from raw data, and assembling deterministic Layer 2 Snapshots that serve as the single source of truth for the entire trading pipeline.

nodes.label: System
nodes.name: Trading Engine
nodes.summary: Bounded context responsible for transforming Layer 2 analytical snapshots into trading decisions, executing orders through broker APIs, managing open positions, and enforcing stop-loss rules.

nodes.label: System
nodes.name: Risk Control
nodes.summary: Bounded context responsible for enforcing hard constraints, tracking portfolio exposure, and providing circuit-breaking capability.

nodes.label: System
nodes.name: Agent Runtime
nodes.summary: Bounded context responsible for agent memory persistence, context window assembly, and trade logging.

nodes.label: System
nodes.name: Evaluation Loop
nodes.summary: Bounded context responsible for evaluating trading performance, validating promotion readiness, and managing the system lifecycle state machine.

nodes.label: System
nodes.name: Supervisor Office
nodes.summary: Bounded context responsible for meta-governance of the trading system: evaluating weaknesses, allocating treasury under policy constraints, selecting and applying upgrades, and orchestrating the agent team.

nodes.summary: Unit tests for the runtime guard predicates (PRED-006/007 + echoes), each in isolation: once-ever dedup (prior ADMIT only), operational preconditions (halt / degraded / not-tradeable / venue-closed / wrong instrument / default-closed), and the snapshot echoes (true / false / default-closed-on-absent).

nodes.label: Test
nodes.name: test_paper_runtime_engine
nodes.summary: Behavioral tests for `evaluate()`: ADMIT / REJECT(duplicate) / REJECT(operational) / HOLD(WATCH) / HOLD(INDETERMINATE), the first-failure-names-the-guard order, the config require-flags, the `supervisor_ok` None stub, the canonical guard-block order, and the `RuntimeDecisionRecord` fail-closed `__post_init__` (ADMIT ⇔ no triggered guard).

nodes.label: Test
nodes.name: test_paper_runtime_determinism
nodes.summary: Determinism + fingerprint-coherence tests: a `RuntimeDecisionRecord` is byte-identical across two `evaluate()` runs from the same prior ledger; `record_id` binds the prior ledger state; the pinned `runtime_policy_fingerprint` (`ab798cae…6f32`) changes on a require-flag edit and is unchanged by a version-only bump; the fingerprint threads into `record_id`.

nodes.label: Test
nodes.name: test_paper_runtime_ledger
nodes.summary: Ledger idempotency + sequence-replay tests: `run_sequence` twice ⇒ identical records + identical ending `state_hash`; a re-presented snapshot ⇒ duplicate / non-ADMIT; `has_admit` counts only ADMITs; append-only immutability + length-derived `seq`; a halted op mid-sequence ⇒ REJECT with the ledger still advancing; `state_hash` stable through serialization; `seq` continuity across persist/reload; default-closed loaders (absent ledger ⇒ empty, absent operational ⇒ closed).

nodes.label: Test
nodes.name: test_paper_runtime_bench
nodes.summary: Tests for the paper-runtime benchmark (BENCH-003): report determinism, both sequences byte-identical, no enrich-back (packet `guard_refs` stay unevaluated), the real re-presented snapshot flagged a duplicate, the synthetic sequence reaching every verdict (ADMIT 3 / HOLD 1 / REJECT 3) with pinned reject attribution, and the committed golden artifact staying in sync.

nodes.label: Test
nodes.name: test_execution_engine
nodes.summary: Behavioral tests for `execute()`: a LONG+approved fill (adverse slippage, mark-to-snapshot P&L), cost-averaging accumulation, the fail-closed no-fill paths (guard block / non-LONG stance / already-executed idempotency), a non-ADMIT input raising, the `GuardResult` + `ExecutionRecord` fail-closed invariants, and `execution_id` binding the prior portfolio state.

nodes.label: Test
nodes.name: test_execution_determinism
nodes.summary: The BENCH-004 core (ADR-011 §2): `run_sequence` twice over the same items + captured guard config yields byte-identical records and an identical ending portfolio `state_hash`; a persist/load round-trip preserves the `state_hash`; a missing portfolio file is the empty state; a repeated `source_snapshot_id` does not double-fill.

nodes.label: Test
nodes.name: test_execution_guards
nodes.summary: The GATE-001 guard-wiring (ADR-011 gate c): `run_guard` maps a `GuardrailEngine` APPROVE/BLOCK to a forwarded `GuardResult`; a block (position-size / withdrawal) yields a no-fill record naming the first failing predicate; the **captured** guard config drives the outcome regardless of the environment (gate c.4 replay determinism).

nodes.label: Test
nodes.name: test_execution_bench
nodes.summary: The Execution Layer Benchmark (BENCH-004) in-sync + determinism test (the BENCH-003 `test_paper_runtime_bench` idiom): the harness is deterministic, every block replays byte-identically, the real sequence is grounded in the real corpus (`952cc83a…`, not invented), the synthetic sequence reaches the full execution outcome space (fill / non-LONG no-fill / idempotent no-double-fill / guard-block attribution), the captured guard configs fingerprint into the replay key, and the committed golden artifact stays in sync (drift ⇒ red).

nodes.label: Test
nodes.name: test_forward_return_labels
nodes.summary: The test suite for the Gold Forward-Return Labeler (MOD-009) and its committed golden Gold Forward-Return Label Set (BENCH-005).

nodes.label: Test
nodes.name: test_chain_engine
nodes.summary: The chain orchestrator core (MOD-010) behavioral test over the real consumable fixture: ADMIT + no-fill on the monochromatic AVOID corpus; the in-hand price/direction forwarding (ADR-011 D1); wrap-not-enrich (the packet stays pure, ADR-009 §2); forwarded snapshot provenance + `as_of`; the GATE-001 guard-wiring with block attribution; the non-ADMIT → no-execute branch; end-to-end idempotency; the fail-closed ADMIT-without-price guard; and bounded-context hygiene (only the orchestrator imports `src/risk`).

nodes.label: Test
nodes.name: test_chain_determinism
nodes.summary: The chain orchestrator determinism + IO round-trip test (MOD-010): byte-identical end-to-end replay through `run_sequence` (all five record types + ending ledger + portfolio state), end-to-end admission idempotency, the captured-input replay invariant (the replay path never reads `os.environ`), and the `run_once` IO shell — persist (portfolio-then-ledger) + reload round-trip, the non-consumable → `None` fail-closed branch, and on-disk idempotency.

nodes.label: Test
nodes.name: test_chain_bench
nodes.summary: The Chain Orchestrator Benchmark (BENCH-006) in-sync + determinism test (the BENCH-004 `test_execution_bench` idiom): the harness is deterministic, the real sequence replays byte-identically across all five record types, the real ADMIT is grounded in the consumable corpus (`952cc83a…`, `packet_id gold-v0:5653d07a0b3949d5`, never invented), the monochromatic-AVOID corpus is an ADMIT-then-idempotent-REJECT no-fill, the full replay key is complete, and the committed golden artifact stays in sync (drift ⇒ red).

nodes.label: Test
nodes.name: test_operational_feed
nodes.summary: The live operational-status feed adapter test (MOD-010 seam, FILE-036): the deterministic `MarketCalendarFeed` (open on a trading day; fail-closed on weekend / weekday-holiday / unparseable / absent), the capture round-trip (the produced `OperationalInput` reloads via `load_operational`), and — the non-negotiable — the **replay-path quarantine**: capture freezes the value at read time and a `run_sequence` replay threads it without ever re-reading the feed (a stub feed's call-count stays at 1).

nodes.label: Test
nodes.name: test_alpaca_clock_feed
nodes.summary: The live Alpaca clock/calendar `OperationalFeed` plug test (MOD-010 seam, FILE-037): the calendar-driven open/closed decision; the **holiday-gap closure** (Good Friday 2026 — a weekday the fixed-date `MarketCalendarFeed` wrongly reports open, `AlpacaClockFeed` correctly reports closed); fail-closed on a client error / missing client / unparseable `as_of`; the `clock_feed_from_env` factory fail-closing on missing creds and **refusing a non-paper base URL** — including spoofed sub-/super-domain, query- and fragment-borne, and non-https URLs (parsed-hostname equality, not a substring match), while accepting a mixed-case paper host; and the **replay-path quarantine** (the captured Alpaca-produced `OperationalInput` reloads via `load_operational` and `run_sequence` threads it without re-reading the feed).

nodes.label: Test
nodes.name: test_alpaca_adapter
nodes.summary: The live Alpaca **paper** `ExecutionPort` plug test (MOD-008 / INT-011, FILE-038): the fill echo (a stub paper order maps to a `Fill` with realized slippage); the determinism-boundary flags (`mode == ALPACA_PAPER`, `replayable is False`); fail-closed on a missing client / non-LONG direction / non-filled order; the `paper_adapter_from_env` factory fail-closing on missing creds and **refusing a non-paper base URL**; and the **quarantine** — through the pure `execute()` engine the adapter stamps `replayable=False` onto the record, a no-fill path never touches the broker, and the default port stays the deterministic `SimulatedBrokerAdapter`.
